# Grade 7 Social Studies Lesson Plan: The Constitutional Convention
Foxglove Middle School - Room 204

## Overview
- Teacher: Frank Hendricks
- Date: 10/14/2026
- Class: Grade 7 Social Studies, Period 3 (50 minutes)
- Unit: Creating the United States Constitution
- Standard: SS.7.CG.1.7 - Explain the compromises made during the Constitutional Convention.
- Essential Question: How did competing interests shape the structure of the national legislature?

## Instructional Materials
- Primary source excerpt: Virginia Plan vs. New Jersey Plan
- Graphic organizer: The Great Compromise comparison chart
- Student response whiteboards and dry-erase markers

## Learning Objectives and Accommodations
| Category | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Target Objective | Students can identify key differences between the Virginia and New Jersey Plans. |
| Student with IEP | Neil Petrov (504 Plan): Provide printed slide notes and 50% extra time on exit ticket. |
| English Learner | Isabel Duarte (ELL Level 2): Visual vocabulary card set provided at desk. |

## Daily Agenda
- 10:00 - 10:08 AM: Bellringer review on the Articles of Confederation.
- 10:08 - 10:25 AM: Direct instruction on the 1787 Philadelphia Convention and legislative representation debates.
- 10:25 - 10:40 AM: Guided partner analysis of the bicameral legislature solution.
- 10:40 - 10:50 AM: Formative assessment.

## Planned Delivery and Checks for Understanding
- During direct instruction, remind students that the New Jersey Plan proposed allocating representation based strictly on state population size.
- Distribute the two-column chart to contrast equal versus proportional representation in the Senate and House.
- Administer the exit ticket during the last 10 minutes to evaluate individual student understanding.
